      <description><![CDATA[Every year, 17.5 lakh Indians die of heart disease. Diabetes and obesity are rising just as fast. And too often, disease is caught when it's already too late.Dr. Shriram Nene spent nearly two decades as a cardiothoracic surgeon fixing hearts in the operating room. Now he wants to keep people from ever getting there.On Young Turks Reloaded, he joins Shereen Bhan to talk about his new book, '21 Days to Good Health', and why medicine has to shift from treating disease late to preventing it early. "Time is muscle. Time is brain," he says.His prescription comes down to five things: diet, exercise, sleep, connections, and stress and mindset. He explains why an hour at the gym can't undo 11 hours of sitting, why muscle loss speeds up after 40, how a 15-minute walk after meals can help, and whether you really need protein supplements. He also covers what data and wearables can and can't tell you, and why women's health has been dangerously neglected.And yes, he didn't know who Madhuri Dixit was when they met.
